name: Git & GitHub Version Control Track
description: Master distributed version control, commit staging, feature branching strategies, interactive rebasing, merge conflict resolution, stashing, and GitHub team pull request workflows.
whatYouLearn: Initialize local Git repositories and configure user identity
Track file state stages (untracked, modified, staged, committed)
Manage feature branches, merging, and merge conflict resolution
Perform interactive rebasing, commit squashing, and cherry-picking
Utilize git stash to temporarily store uncommitted working changes
Execute team GitHub Pull Request code review workflows

exercises.title: Repository Initialization & Global Identity Config
exercises.description: Configure user name/email and initialize a local Git repository.
exercises.theory: Git tracks history by author identity. Configure global user.name and user.email before initializing repositories with git init.
exercises.objective: Set global user configuration and initialize a new Git repository.
exercises.initialCode: # Configure user identity and initialize repository
exercises.solutionCode:
git config --global user.name "Alex River"
git config --global user.email "alex@bytecode.io"
git config --global init.defaultBranch main

git init bytecode-app
cd bytecode-app
git status
requirements: Set git config --global user.name and user.email
Initialize repository using git init bytecode-app
Inspect initial repository state with git status
hints: git status displays active branch, staged files, and untracked files

exercises.title: Staging & Committing Files (git add, git commit)
exercises.description: Stage modified files into the index and record atomic commits.
exercises.theory: Git uses a 3-tier architecture: Working Directory -> Staging Index -> Commit History. Use git add to stage files and git commit -m to save snapshot history.
exercises.objective: Stage new files and create an initial commit.
exercises.solutionCode:
echo "

ByteCode

" > index.html git add index.html git commit -m "feat: initialize HTML document structure" git log --oneline
requirements: Stage index.html using git add
Create commit with conventional commit message git commit -m 'feat: ...'
Inspect commit history using git log --oneline
hints: git add . stages all modified and untracked files in current directory

exercises.title: Inspecting Differences & History (git diff, git log)
exercises.description: Compare working directory changes and inspect formatted commit logs.
exercises.theory: git diff compares working directory changes against the staging index. git log displays commit history graphs.
exercises.objective: Inspect file modifications using git diff.
exercises.initialCode: # Compare modified changes with git diff
exercises.solutionCode:
echo "

New feature paragraph

" >> index.html git diff git add index.html git diff --staged git commit -m "docs: update feature section"
requirements: Use git diff to view unstaged working directory changes
Use git diff --staged to view staged changes before commit
hints: git diff --staged displays differences between staged index and last commit

exercises.title: Ignoring Unwanted Files (.gitignore)
exercises.description: Exclude node_modules, build artifacts, and secrets using .gitignore.
exercises.theory: The .gitignore file defines pattern rules matching files and directories that Git should never track or commit.
exercises.objective: Create a .gitignore file ignoring node_modules and .env files.
exercises.solutionCode:
cat <<EOT > .gitignore
node_modules/
dist/
.env
*.log
EOT

git add .gitignore
git commit -m "chore: add .gitignore configuration"
requirements: Ignore node_modules/ directory
Ignore .env secrets file and *.log files
Commit .gitignore file
hints: Directories end with trailing slash node_modules/

exercises.title: Branch Creation & Switching (git branch, git checkout / switch)
exercises.description: Create isolated feature branches and switch branch contexts.
exercises.theory: Branches allow developing features in isolated environments without affecting the main production branch. git switch switches active branch context.
exercises.objective: Create and switch to a new feature branch.
exercises.solutionCode:
git switch -c feature/user-auth

echo "// Auth module" > auth.js
git add auth.js
git commit -m "feat: implement auth login handler"

git switch main
requirements: Create and switch branch using git switch -c feature/user-auth
Commit changes on feature branch
Switch back to main branch using git switch main
hints: git switch -c branch-name creates and checks out new branch in single command
exercises.codeExample: git switch -c feature/login; git switch main;

exercises.title: Branch Merging (Fast-Forward vs 3-Way Merge)
exercises.description: Merge completed feature branches back into the main line of development.
exercises.theory: git merge integrates history from a target branch into active branch. Fast-forward merges simply move the branch pointer forward.
exercises.objective: Merge feature branch into main using git merge.
exercises.solutionCode:
git switch main
git merge feature/user-auth -m "merge: integrate user-auth feature branch"
git branch -d feature/user-auth
git branch
requirements: Switch to main branch
Merge feature/user-auth branch
Delete merged feature branch using git branch -d
hints: git branch -d deletes branch safely after it has been merged
exercises.codeExample: git checkout main; git merge feature/login;

exercises.title: Resolving Merge Conflicts
exercises.description: Identify conflict markers (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>) and resolve merge conflicts.
exercises.theory: Merge conflicts occur when changes are made to the same lines of a file in two different branches. Resolving requires manually editing conflict markers.
exercises.objective: Resolve a simulated file merge conflict manually.
exercises.solutionCode:
# Manually resolve file conflict cat < index.html

ByteCode Combined Header

EOT git add index.html git commit -m "fix: resolve merge conflict between main and feature branch"
requirements: Remove conflict markers <<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>
Combine conflicting content lines cleanly
Stage resolved file with git add and complete merge commit
hints: Staging resolved files with git add marks conflict as resolved

exercises.title: Stashing Changes (git stash, pop, list)
exercises.description: Temporarily shelve uncommitted dirty working directory changes using git stash.
exercises.theory: git stash saves uncommitted modifications to a temporary stack, returning working directory to clean HEAD state.
exercises.objective: Stash uncommitted work, switch context, and restore stashed work.
exercises.solutionCode:
echo "// Unfinished draft code" >> app.js

git stash save "WIP: unfinished app logic"
git stash list

# Perform urgent hotfix on clean HEAD

git stash pop
requirements: Stash working changes with git stash save 'msg'
Inspect stash list using git stash list
Restore changes using git stash pop
hints: git stash pop applies stashed changes and deletes item from stash stack

exercises.title: Undoing Changes (git checkout, restore, reset)
exercises.description: Discard unstaged modifications or unstage files using git restore and git reset.
exercises.theory: git restore discards unstaged working tree changes. git restore --staged un-stages files without losing file edits.
exercises.objective: Unstage staged file and discard working directory edits.
exercises.solutionCode:
echo "Bad Edits" >> app.js
git add app.js

# Unstage file
git restore --staged app.js

# Discard working tree changes
git restore app.js

git status
requirements: Unstage staged file using git restore --staged
Discard working directory changes using git restore
hints: git restore replaces working file content with latest commit version
exercises.codeExample: git restore --staged file.js; git restore file.js;

exercises.title: Interactive Rebasing (git rebase -i)
exercises.description: Squash, edit, and reword commit history using interactive rebase.
exercises.theory: Interactive rebase (git rebase -i HEAD~N) cleans commit history by squashing multiple small fix commits into single logical commits.
exercises.objective: Rebase and squash 3 commits into 1 clean commit.
exercises.solutionCode:
# Rebase interactive command simulation
# In interactive editor, mark commits 2 and 3 as 'squash' or 's'
# Pick commit 1: pick 1234567 feat: initial implementation
# Squash commit 2: s 89abcde fix typo
# Squash commit 3: s ffedcba fix formatting

git rebase -i HEAD~3
requirements: Run git rebase -i HEAD~3
Use 'squash' or 's' on secondary commits to combine history
hints: Never rebase commits that have already been pushed to public shared branches

exercises.title: Cherry-Picking Commits (git cherry-pick)
exercises.description: Apply specific commit SHA hash changes from one branch onto active branch.
exercises.theory: git cherry-pick <commit-hash> applies the exact change introduced by a specific commit from another branch onto the active branch.
exercises.objective: Cherry-pick a bugfix commit from a hotfix branch onto main.
exercises.solutionCode:
git switch main
git cherry-pick a1b2c3d4
git log --oneline -n 1
requirements: Switch to main branch
Apply specified commit hash using git cherry-pick <hash>
hints: Cherry-picking creates a new commit on active branch containing identical patch changes

exercises.title: Remote Repositories (git remote, push, pull, fetch)
exercises.description: Connect local repository to GitHub remote origin and synchronize changes.
exercises.theory: git remote manages connections to remote repository servers (GitHub). git fetch downloads remote commits without merging.
exercises.objective: Add remote origin and push main branch.
exercises.solutionCode:
git remote add origin https://github.com/bytecode/app.git
git remote -v

# Fetch remote tracking branches
git fetch origin

# Push main branch and set upstream tracking
git push -u origin main
requirements: Add remote origin using git remote add origin <url>
Inspect remotes using git remote -v
Push branch and set upstream using git push -u origin main
hints: -u (--set-upstream) binds local branch to remote tracking branch
exercises.codeExample: git remote add origin <url>; git push -u origin main;

exercises.title: Git Tags & Semantic Versioning (git tag)
exercises.description: Create annotated release tags matching semantic versioning standards (v1.0.0).
exercises.theory: Git tags create indelible markers pointing to specific commit milestones in project history, commonly used for release versions.
exercises.objective: Create annotated release tag v1.0.0 and push tags to remote.
exercises.solutionCode:
git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "Release v1.0.0: Initial Production Release"
git tag -l
git push origin v1.0.0
requirements: Create annotated tag using git tag -a v1.0.0 -m 'msg'
List tags with git tag -l
Push tag using git push origin v1.0.0
hints: Annotated tags storing tagger identity and date are preferred over lightweight tags for software releases
exercises.codeExample: git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "Release"; git push origin --tags;

exercises.title: Git Reflog & Recovering Lost Commits
exercises.description: Recover deleted branches or lost commits using git reflog.
exercises.theory: git reflog logs every HEAD update in local repository, allowing recovery of reset or deleted commits.
exercises.objective: Recover a reset commit using git reflog and git reset.
exercises.solutionCode:
git reflog

# Locate HEAD@{n} commit SHA before reset occurred
# Reset branch back to recovered commit hash
git reset --hard HEAD@{1}
requirements: Inspect reflog history using git reflog
Recover lost commit state using git reset --hard HEAD@{n}
hints: reflog keeps track of local actions even after hard resets or branch deletions

exercises.title: GitHub Pull Requests & Code Review
exercises.description: Create feature branches and open GitHub Pull Requests for team code review.
exercises.theory: GitHub Pull Requests (PRs) allow developers to notify team members of completed feature branches for code review before merging.
exercises.objective: Push feature branch and prepare pull request submission.
exercises.solutionCode:
git switch -c feature/payment-gateway

echo "// Payment logic" > payment.js
git add payment.js
git commit -m "feat: implement payment gateway integration"

git push -u origin feature/payment-gateway
requirements: Create feature branch feature/payment-gateway
Commit feature implementation
Push branch to remote origin with -u
hints: Once branch is pushed, GitHub URL prompt displays direct link to open Pull Request

exercises.title: Git Hooks (pre-commit, pre-push)
exercises.description: Automate linting and unit test execution using Client-Side Git Hooks.
exercises.theory: Git hooks are custom scripts located inside .git/hooks/ that run automatically before or after Git lifecycle events (commit, push).
exercises.objective: Create an executable pre-commit hook script.
exercises.solutionCode:
cat <<EOT > .git/hooks/pre-commit
#!/bin/sh
echo "[Git Hook]: Running pre-commit validation tests..."
# Execute test or linter command
# exit 1 to abort commit if tests fail
exit 0
EOT

chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
requirements: Write pre-commit script inside .git/hooks/pre-commit
Set executable permissions using chmod +x
hints: Returning exit code 1 from pre-commit hook aborts the commit action

exercises.title: Git Submodules
exercises.description: Embed external Git repositories as submodules inside parent projects.
exercises.theory: Git submodules allow keeping a Git repository as a subdirectory of another Git repository at a fixed commit hash.
exercises.objective: Add and initialize a Git submodule repository.
exercises.solutionCode:
git submodule add https://github.com/bytecode/shared-utils.git vendor/shared-utils
git submodule update --init --recursive

git add .gitmodules vendor/shared-utils
git commit -m "chore: add shared-utils submodule"
requirements: Add submodule with git submodule add <url> <path>
Initialize submodules using git submodule update --init --recursive
hints: .gitmodules file records path mapping to remote submodule URLs

exercises.title: Git Bisect (Debugging Regression Commits)
exercises.description: Locate the exact commit that introduced a bug using binary search with git bisect.
exercises.theory: git bisect performs binary search across commit history to pinpoint which specific commit introduced a bug regression.
exercises.objective: Run git bisect to identify faulty commit hash.
exercises.solutionCode:
git bisect start
git bisect bad                 # Current HEAD contains bug
git bisect good v1.0.0         # v1.0.0 tag was known good

# Test commit, then mark as good or bad:
# git bisect good OR git bisect bad

git bisect reset               # End bisect session
requirements: Start session with git bisect start
Mark current state git bisect bad and known good commit git bisect good <hash>
Reset when complete with git bisect reset
hints: git bisect automates binary search, reducing manual debugging from hundreds of commits to ~7 steps
exercises.codeExample: git bisect start; git bisect bad; git bisect good <tag>;

exercises.title: Git Blame & History Inspection
exercises.description: Inspect author and commit details line-by-line using git blame.
exercises.theory: git blame annotates every line of a file with the commit hash, author, and date of the last modification.
exercises.objective: Inspect line-by-line author history for a file.
exercises.solutionCode:
git blame app.js

# Inspect specific line range 10 to 20
git blame -L 10,20 app.js
requirements: Run git blame on file
Use -L line range option to restrict output
hints: -L 10,20 limits output to lines 10 through 20

exercises.title: Capstone Project: Production Git Team Workflow Strategy
exercises.description: Execute a complete Git feature branch, rebasing, squashing, merge conflict resolution, and release tagging workflow.
exercises.theory: This capstone exercise synthesizes professional Git engineering: Branching strategy, atomic staging, squashing commits, resolving merge conflicts, and tagging semantic version releases.
exercises.objective: Execute complete release workflow script.
exercises.solutionCode:
# 1. Feature Branch Creation
git switch -c feature/payment-stripe

echo "stripe_key=sk_test_123" > stripe.env
git add stripe.env
git commit -m "feat: add stripe environment configuration"

echo "// Stripe Client" > stripe.js
git add stripe.js
git commit -m "feat: implement stripe payment client"

# 2. Interactive Squash & Rebase onto main
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch feature/payment-stripe
git rebase main

# 3. Fast-Forward Merge into main & Release Tag
git switch main
git merge feature/payment-stripe
git tag -a v2.0.0 -m "Release v2.0.0 with Stripe Payment Support"

# 4. Clean up
git branch -d feature/payment-stripe
git log --oneline -n 5
requirements: Create feature branch and make atomic commits
Rebase feature branch onto updated main branch
Merge into main and tag semantic release v2.0.0
hints: Rebasing before merging creates a linear, clean commit history
exercises.codeExample: git switch main; git merge feature; git tag v1.0.0;
